messages.content:
Risk: Compromised personally identifiable information
Description: The AI system may expose personally identifiable information (PII), either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. PII is any data that can be used to directly identify or contact a specific individual, either alone or in combination with other information.
Concern: None
Policy: Protected Health Information and Data Privacy

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0001872: extent of AE recovery — an information content entity that represents an extent of recovery from an adverse event [found by 5/15 queries]
  Siblings: DIPS question, directive information entity, patient symptom report
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0001565: adverse event filtering cutoff — a data item that represents a threshold cutoff for filtering out those adverse event case reports that are unlikely important for a specific AE study. This is applied to the analysis of AE case resport data in an AE case reporting system such as FAERS or VAERS. [found by 5/15 queries]
  Siblings: clinical finding, adverse event causality score, AE incidence rate
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 11/15 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HealthDataExposure: Health Data Exposure — Unauthorized disclosure of protected health information including medical records, diagnoses, treatments, or prescription histories. [found by 9/15 queries]
  Siblings: Unauthorized Surveillance, Direct Identifier Exposure, Employment Data Exposure
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DirectIdentifierExposure: Direct Identifier Exposure — Disclosure of information that directly identifies individuals, such as names, addresses, government identifiers, or biometric data. [found by 9/15 queries]
  Siblings: Unauthorized Surveillance, Health Data Exposure, Employment Data Exposure

axes.rationale: This class directly maps to the core of the risk: the exposure of specific identifiers (names, addresses, etc.) that constitute PII.
Since the risk involves PII and mentions protected health information in the policy context, this class provides a specific dimension of the type of sensitive data being compromised.
